articles.title: Hackers Use ConnectWise SkyKick Credentials to Access Microsoft 365, Halting Cloud Backups
articles.summary:
Attackers abused compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credentials to access Microsoft 365 customer environments, prompting ConnectWise to shut off application access and interrupt backup services. Jonathan Semon confirmed unauthorized sign-ins across 162 tenants as of 19:00 UTC on October 16, exposing risks associated with privileged vendor applications. articles.title: Critical WordPress Flaws Allow Attackers to Execute Remote Code Without Authentication
articles.summary:
Two WordPress Core vulnerabilities can be chained to execute remote code without authentication, according to analysis by Seqrite researcher Amruta Wagh. Dubbed WP2Shell, the exploit chain reportedly emerged in July 2026 and combines REST API route confusion with SQL injection, allowing attackers to progress from public endpoints to server compromise without possessing valid WordPress credentials. articles.title: GhostAction Hackers Hide Credential-Stealing Malware in Fake Font Files Across 94 GitHub Repositories
articles.summary:

Jenn Gile identified 94 compromised repositories belonging to 66 owners, confirming the payload in all 79 repositories available for analysis. The remaining 15 were inaccessible. […]

articles.title: SideCopy Hackers Target Indian Organizations With ReverseRAT Malware to Steal Data
articles.summary:

articles.title: New GhostBat Android Malware Targets 60 Banking and UPI Apps to Steal PINs
articles.summary:
A new GhostBat RAT variant targets 60 Android financial application packages used in India, combining accessibility-based PIN capture with a transparent overlay that intercepts interactions inside legitimate Google Pay and MobiKwik interfaces. The findings extend Cyble’s October 2025 investigation, which documented GhostBat spreading through fraudulent mParivahan applications, harvesting banking messages, and stealing UPI PINs through […]

articles.title: Midnight Blizzard-Linked Malware Server Still Delivering Payloads 8 Weeks After Disclosure
articles.summary:

articles.title: Android Malware Exposes Its Own Operators While Hijacking Phones and Stealing Sensitive Data
articles.summary:
An Android remote-access Trojan, YuanKong, whose weakly protected dropper reveals more than its hidden payload: it exposes the operator account identifiers embedded in each build. Analysis of 110 droppers uncovered 57 distinct child payloads, 42 operator accounts and 44 rotating build brands, all tied together by a shared signing certificate and command-and-control (C2) infrastructure.
